study.question: Does explicit breadth of supplied category/brand IDs complement event volume, and is any incremental predictive value specific to activity strictly newer than the inherited crossed-field match anchor?
study.hypothesis: Observed source limitation: incumbent scalar summaries count events, compare ages, and pool embeddings, but have no explicit cardinality of distinct receiving-field IDs. Event counts alone alias repeated activity on one ID with activity across several IDs. The learned embedding pool might already recover sufficient breadth; this is unresolved, not an observed predictive failure. r0023 newer count improves AUC over its duplicate control by only 0.00008783094, and every r0024 provenance extension is below its parent; signed provenance-by-volume is therefore unsupported in that implementation. Conditional on the unchanged parent representation, a deterministic distinct-ID count may expose breadth complementary to volume. The newer-than-anchor restriction might localize that information; this requires a factorial contrast, not an assumption that it wins. Distinct supplied IDs are a coarse category/brand breadth measure, not item diversity, intent or negative preference.

nearest_work.difference: DIN already motivates diverse interests and preserves intensity through unnormalized learned activation. We inherit a normalized, field-adapted attention model and deterministic intensity summaries; test an additional exact ID-cardinality readout at fixed event volume and support. This is neither original DIN reproduction nor a verified novelty claim.

README establishes category/brand/action histories without item IDs. Use supplied category/brand IDs only. Publisher full text unavailable: no detailed DMR mechanism comparison or priority claim is possible.

Retain the complete count/ordinal parent, append eight columns measuring distinct IDs versus repeated event counts in matched all/newer populations. Sorting is only an exact set-cardinality implementation, not a new input or chronological assumption.

No signed same/fallback routing is added. Their nearly identical AUCs and failure to beat the parent motivate a different source of information rather than declaring provenance or count mechanisms refuted.

inherited_components: All incumbent embeddings, normalized shared category/brand attention and blind static context queries
All 27 incumbent non-forward/non-diagnostic helper methods, including causal count/decay, pair support, extrema, crossed ordinal rank, pooled fallback, latest-activity frontier and newer-event count
All original constructor statements and random initialization draws, original hidden widths [128,64], Adam/lr0.001, frozen epochs3/batch4096/history128/train seed42/data passes
Fixed pooled support P and crossed same-action anchor with pooled-action fallback; receiving-field activity includes target matches as in the parent, not only rivals
study.proposed_difference: Append eight first-layer inputs 0.5*log1p(K)/log(129), one per receiving field/action, with zero initial weights. K is either distinct positive supplied IDs or event count, in either all valid receiving-field activity or the strict-newer subset relative to the exact parent anchor. Keep the same inherited support gate P for all four cells, even where strict-newer count is zero. Count distinct IDs separately per action and field; do not deduplicate the parent history or embeddings. All cells compute all four alternatives through identical vectorized sorting. No extra learned embeddings, supervision, optimizer changes, new random draws, history extension or per-seed overrides.
predictions: Primary breadth contrast: validation AUC(distinct_newer) > AUC(events_newer); secondary Logloss and cost must be reported even when discordant. No preset minimum effect or significance claim from one selected seed.

Generic breadth contrast: AUC(distinct_all)-AUC(events_all). Temporal specificity requires the difference-in-differences [distinct_newer-events_newer]-[distinct_all-events_all] > 0; an all-activity gain alone supports only generic breadth.

Source-level identities: distinct_newer <= newer_events; distinct_all <= all_events; distinct_newer <= distinct_all; computed event totals equal inherited burst counts; extra features zero off P, on empty history and on either missing target.

Exact duplication of an event leaves both distinct counts invariant while increasing event count; permuting events or bijectively renaming positive IDs with targets preserves cardinality. These are representation properties, not predictive mechanism evidence.

Candidate-supplied first512 diagnostics should measure repeated-ID prevalence before interpreting any gain. Such probes are exploratory, unrepresentative and cannot establish full-population support or causal meaning.
falsifiers: Neither distinct cell beats its matched event-count control: no support for this explicit breadth implementation. A null newer comparison with a positive all comparison falsifies temporal-specificity, not generic breadth.
Distinct_newer fails to improve the current parent or its apparent advantage vanishes across future paired seeds: no supported performance advance.

Event counts already equal distinct counts on relevant populations, or probe support is negligible: the proposed representation difference is locally absent or weak; do not infer a mechanism from a tiny selected AUC difference.

Broken cardinality inequalities, parent-prefix or count reconstruction identities, missing/empty leakage, nonfinite host tensors/logits/diagnostics, or cap overrun invalidate the relevant implementation rather than refuting breadth.
alternative_explanations: Added duplicate readout changes optimization; events_newer duplicates an existing count and has identical parameter budget, initialization and generic sorting cost.
Any breadth improvement may reflect general activity concentration rather than evidence after target relevance; the all-activity pair tests this.
Coarse or aliased supplied IDs, missing-field patterns, count compression and history truncation can affect apparent breadth; no raw item diversity or intent claim is justified.
The parent embedding pool may encode breadth already; an explicit readout can help optimization without adding raw information.

Adaptive validation selection across 102 previous trajectories, seed variation, user-cluster dependence and sample-specific diagnostics can explain small improvements. No confidence interval or independent repetition is available in this phase.
Sorting increases measured cost and may exceed cap; matched-pass comparisons do not imply equal-compute superiority.

held_fixed: Support P, crossed same-action anchor/fallback, receiving-field/action validity and strict age comparison
Eight zero columns, gain0.5, log1p/log129 scale, parameter count and RNG draws

Selected single seed; no full-population mechanism labels
contrasts.decision_if_supported: Compare parent and all-activity contrast, inspect diagnostics/cost and prioritize paired validation repetition before a breadth mechanism claim.
contrasts.decision_if_not_supported: Retain negative result; compare all-activity cell to distinguish window mismatch from a null cardinality readout. Do not repeat identical seeds as mechanism contrasts.

held_fixed: All parent representations and causal information boundary
All receiving action/field populations before window selection
Inherited support gate and shared logcount scaling
Capacity, initialization, computed alternatives and frozen training recipe

contrasts.decision_if_supported: Temporal-specificity is provisionally supported only if breadth contrast is positive and larger for newer than all; repeat the consequential cells with paired seeds at final validation.
contrasts.decision_if_not_supported: Report generic breadth only if all contrast is positive; if both null/negative, prefer parent and investigate reproducibility of r0023 count increment rather than adding interactions.
